candidates.name: Restroom Stalls and All LLC (RSA)
candidates.partition_evidence: Its site offers sales, distribution and installation of toilet partitions, done by its own W2 crews in GA, FL, AL, TN, SC and NC. It lists commercial projects including a stadium, hospitals and universities.
red_flags: Sells partitions itself, so it could buy around us
About 190 miles from Huntsville, beyond the 120-mile regional limit
candidates.reason: A proven commercial partition installer that says it installs in Alabama with its own crews. It is based about 190 miles away and is also a partition seller, so it is a fallback rather than a strong local pick.

license.name: Restroom Stalls and All LLC (RSA)
license.registry: Alabama Licensing Board for General Contractors, full license roster
license.note: Checked 2026-11-20. The Alabama GC Board roster CSV has no entry with 'Restroom', 'Stalls' or 'RSA' in the name. None of the Gainesville, GA licensees on the roster is this company. Alabama needs this license only for jobs of $100,000 or more (genconbd.alabama.gov, per repo state research), so most partition installs don't need it. Huntsville isn't one of the 99 areas in the repo's local-rules research, so no city rule was checked. The company's home-state Georgia board lookup (verify.sos.ga.gov) returned HTTP 403.

license.name: 3rd Gen LLC
license.registry: Alabama Licensing Board for General Contractors license roster (licensesearch.alabama.gov/genconbd)
license.note: Checked 2026-11-20. The board's public roster (about 11,100 entries, all embedded in the page) has no entry for '3rd Gen' or 'Third Gen' and no matching firm in Hartselle. Alabama requires a general contractor license only for jobs at or above the state threshold ($50,000 commercial). Huntsville has no local installer rule, so a typical partition job below that amount needs no state license. The company site (https://3rdgenpro.com) shows the name '3rd Gen LLC' in the footer and lists bath hardware, shower enclosures, mirrors and shelving across Northern Alabama and Central Tennessee. The site does not mention toilet partitions or give a license number. Its base city is not stated there.
